I read aloud this book I grew up with, Stone Soup, by Ann McGovern, illustrated by Winslow Pinney Pels. I also attempt a cooking experiment to make soup from a spoon! And it works! 

It's the story of a young hungry traveler who stops at a little house to see if he might get something to eat. But the old woman inside tells him there is nothing in the house and nothing in the garden. So he asks her for a stone. The befuddled woman is amazed to see what this young man has in mind with a stone since rocks are not edible. This leads to one thing after another being added to the pot till a delicious meal is prepared and the table is set for both parties to dine like royalty. This caused me to wonder if I could make stone soup on my own and if it might be a fun cooking activity that could bring your family closer together. 

Rather than recommend the use of stones, since leached chemicals, strange minerals, and bacteria could be a problem, I thought instead I would show how to make an equally wonderful treat, SPOON SOUP! The good thing about Spoon Soup is that you get to eat the soup with the spoon you used to start the pot boiling. 
The ingredients from the book are simply, 
one pot of boiling water 
some onions 
a few carrots 
some beef bones 
salt and a bit of pepper 
and last of all, some barley and butter to help thicken the soup. 

Now you don't have to keep to these ingredients. I added some hot sauce and garlic powder to mine and some whipping cream, but you might add some celery, potatoes, mushrooms, thyme, sage, or different types of meat to your soup. You could also add noodles or rice or beans or tomato paste to it for different flavors. 

Now I also made a Tabouli salad that was just wonderful garnished on top of the soup. I learned how to make it from a low-carbohydrate specialized Doctor named Dr. Sten Eckberg here on YouTube. 
This is the link to his video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hquhxbWHeak 

The ingredients are simply 
50 grams of parsley or about half a bunch, 
half of an onion or maybe less than that even if you don't want it too strong, 
half or more of a diced lemon, not squeezed. 
I think it could do with a whole lemon, 
salt to taste, 
and 1/4 cup of extra virgin olive oil. 
Oh and most importantly, 50 grams of chopped pecans.

It's a delicious garnish for steak or soup or anything savory like that. I hope you enjoy this video and that it sparks some creativity in your kitchen, but more importantly, sparks some attitude adjustment in your children to see that sometimes we glance around ourselves like the old woman in the story and think there's nothing good around us. There's nothing to eat or nothing to do and nothing to be excited about. 

Not true! 

All we need to do is learn to be creative and make something more out of our day with the things we have at our fingertips. I think that's the moral with this one. The young man's superpower is helping motivate other people to try things and to build their enthusiasm. You'll notice he doesn't force the old woman to help him. She helps make the soup out of curiosity. 

Anyway, I had a great time making this soup today and it really did turn out fantastically. If you're wondering about the fat content, it was very high. I've gone off sugar the last year. The barley in the soup today was one of the higher carbohydrate things I've eaten all year. I've lost about 60 pounds. If you're still eating a lot of carbohydrates, I'd avoid putting so much butter and cream in the soup since insulin will cause you to store the fat. If you want to look into what I've done, look for any videos with Dr. Jason Fung, Dr. Ben Bikman, Dr. Sten Eckberg, Dr. Shawn Baker, or Dr. Ken Berry. The journalistic work of Nina Teicholz is also very helpful. That's the advice I began following a year ago and I've seen a miracle in my life since adopting an extremely low-carbohydrate diet. It's not necessary if your body is metabolically flexible, but if you have trouble losing weight, or are diabetic, insulin resistance is worth learning about so you can figure out a way to improve your health. Thank you so much for watching! 

Music in this episode was Cooper Cannell -  Muffin Man (Free music), and [Electro Swing] Odd Chap - Vintage Jukebox EP Mix

Big Bad Bruce
by Bill Peet
Bruce is a big mean bear who loves nothing more than wreaking havoc on the forest tossing boulders down hills smashing trees to smithereens and making the small woodland creatures go running and flapping for their lives. This makes him laugh and laugh! But then he tosses a boulder just a little too close to a witch out picking blueberries. She stomps up the hill to yell at him but he just laughs and saunters off. So she goes home to her cottage to make a pie for him, a magic spell pie with a magic potion inside. She sneaks back to the hill and sets it out for Bruce who smells it and comes and gobbles up the whole thing. She warns him but he ignores her and goes off to take a nap. During his nap he shrinks to the size of a chipmunk! He wakes to a terrible nightmare where every animal he used to torment is now big enough to chase and hurt him. So he runs and runs and finally ends up almost drowning in a small creek. Then nighttime brings owls and other scary beasts into his life. That’s when the witch finds him again and takes him home. But instead of making him disappear or hurting him, she keeps him as a wonderful little bear pet and he soon forgets being a big bear and enjoys his life at her house being her pet sleeping with the cat under the warm stove and tossing pebbles in the garden to scare the bugs and crickets like he used to do to the squirrels and rabbits and quail in the forest. 

This is a fun little story that I hope makes your kids smile. Bill Peet was an artist for Walt Disney during the golden age of 2d animation. His books are richly written and beautifully illustrated in a distinctively Bill Peet style. His books are a great source for children who want to learn to draw. 

This is a fun little Halloween story about animals and magic and all the unexpected things that could happen in the forest.

title: The Lorax - By Dr. Seuss - Read Aloud Bedtime Story
fulltitle: The Lorax - By Dr. Seuss - Read Aloud Bedtime Story
description:
In this story, a young boy goes to discover what happened to this poor desolate place where nothing good grows and no animals live except old crows. He meets the Onceler and pays him to hear the story of how this once beautiful place became the desert that it is.  There follows the story of the onceler as he came to this place and discovered the Truffula trees. He begins to harvest these for his Thneeds, a sweater with connected up sleeves that he can sell for $3.98. He calls his whole family to come to move in and help and altogether they expand and enlarge the business without caring for any of the management of their resources. They chop down the trees without replanting. They wipe out the barbaloot population by destroying the truffula fruit yields. They destroy the air quality with their factory and choke out all the swamiswans so those have to leave. Then they gum up the pond with gobs of brown goo and the fish have to crawl out and leave. And then last of all, they run out of truffula trees because they didn't plant any as they went along. Once that’s done, they all leave except the old onceler. And that’s why the place looks so terrible. 

This story is about mankind’s stewardship over the Earth and the natural resources we have here. It’s a fun rhyming story that I enjoyed when I was little. I hope you like it too!

title: How I Became a Pirate - Read Aloud + Drawing Time
fulltitle: How I Became a Pirate - Read Aloud + Drawing Time
description:
Come on a great adventure with Jeremy Jacob as he meets Captain Braidbeard and his motley crew of pirates! Welcome aboard! Pirates get to skip the vegetables at dinner. They get to play and sing and laugh and throw things and play soccer and never have to go to bed until they want to! It sounds like paradise, but as it turns out, life aboard a pirate ship turns out not to be as much fun as it sounds. There's no one to tuck you in at night and when the ship rocks in a storm, there's no one to hold you and tell you it will be alright. So instead of staying with the pirates, Jeremy shows them where to bury their treasure ( in his back yard) and returns home to live happily ever after. 

This was a fun story to put together. I've included a special drawing time at the end of the show to help your children get started drawing their own sharks and pirates. Hope you enjoy it and keep imagining what wonderful things you could be doing as a pirate!

title: Bartholomew and the Oobleck - By Dr  Seuss -  Read Aloud  - Bedtime Story
fulltitle: Bartholomew and the Oobleck - By Dr  Seuss -  Read Aloud  - Bedtime Story
description:
See what happens when good old King Derwin from the Kingdom of Didd decides he's tired of the normal things that come out of his sky like the rain, the snow, the fog, and the sun. He wants something new. So with a little help from his royal magicians, he has a new type of precipitation brought in. Oobleck, is a green and sticky and terrible substance that gums up birds in their nests and bells in their belfries. As the storm gets worse what began as little drops of oobleck turn into bigger and bigger lumps and slops till all the villagers and farmers are unable to move! The pounding torrents of oobleck outside begin to break the palace's windows and doors, causing all of Bartholomew's friends terrible trouble! It's not until King Derwin learns to apologize that anything improves for his people. This is a sequel to the popular story, The 500 Hats of Bartholomew Cubbins. I've made a video of that book as well that can be found at this link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nPmCRrxMQ9w&t=120s 

This is a story about leadership, handling mistakes, and apology and forgiveness. It teaches children about redemption and that it's important to acknowledge and communicate understanding when you realize you've done something wrong. It shows the power of learning and growing and the terrible consequences that can come when you won't change course down a path that leads to ruin. It's an insightful metaphor written decades ago about a human condition that still very much affects all of us on Earth. Human beings make mistakes. Sometimes we have bad ideas. We may think they're wonderful ideas that can make everything in the world better because it will be different than before, but then we learn that newer isn't necessarily better. And sometimes we can take a course that needs a drastic change back to a more traditional view. This is part of being a person. Being able to apologize and change course is an important skill that will bless people's lives. We have to learn from the world around us and respond. So I thought I'd share this book in this reading so that you could enjoy it. I've added a lot of fun sound effects and tried to create the proper atmosphere for this story to feel real. Maybe it can spur some reluctant readers, to try some longer stories like this. It can be daunting reading bigger words with more on a page, but the story is that much richer when you add it all up.

But now, as the sun rose, Bartholomew smiled. Those silly magicians hadn't done a thing! Then suddenly Bartholomew Cubbins  stopped smiling. Was he seeing things...? No! there was something strange up there in the sky! At first, it seemed like a little greenish cloud... just a wisp of greenish steam. But now it was  coming lower, closer, down toward the fields and farms and houses of the sleeping little kingdom. It was swirling around the topmost turrets of the palace! I'm going to make it a holiday! I want every man, woman, and child in my kingdom to go out and dance in my glorious oobleck!" "Out in that stuff...? " asked  Bartholomew. "Do you really think it's safe Sire?" "Stop asking foolish questions!" snapped the King. "Boy, you run to my royal bell tower. Wake up my royal bell ringer. Tell him to ring the great holiday bell!" He shoved his cold trumpet right into his sleepy  hands. "Get up! Warn the people! Blow the alarm!" "Alarm...?" yawned the trumpeter. Then his eyes saw the  oobleck. "Those green things, Bartholomew! "I'll get the king's horse! I'll ride through the  country! I'll warn the people of the kingdom myself!" He pushed open the door that let out the  Royal Stables. Oh no! (lightning) Bartholomew stopped. He could go no farther. That awful oobleck was  plumping down as big as greenish footballs now! (Sploosh! Boof! Kabloosh!) Too late to warn the people of the kingdom! There  were farmers in the fields, getting stuck to hoes and plows. Goats were getting stuck to ducks. Geese were getting stuck to cows. Outside the palace, it was piling up, great greenish tons of oobleck, deeper and deeper on every roof in the land. There was nothing Bartholomew Cubbins could do out there. Shaking his head sadly, he stepped back inside. (heavy thudding) But inside, a moment later, it was just as bad as  out! With an angry roar, the oobleck was suddenly hitting the palace harder. It was battering and spattering against the walls as big as greenish buckets full of gooey asparagus  soup! Like a sinking sailboat, the whole palace was springing leaks. The oobleck was  ripping the windows right off their hinges. (Crashing and Sloshing) It was dripping through the ceilings. It was  rolling down the chimneys. It was coming in everywhere... even through the keyholes! From every bedroom in the palace came the howls of lords and ladies. Frightened, in their nightgowns, they  came jumping to their doors. "Go back to your beds! Get under your blankets!" Bartholomew  Cubbins went crying through the halls.   But nobody paid the slightest attention. Everyone  in the palace started rushing madly about. Oh no!!! The Royal Cook rushed down to the Royal Kitchen. Bartholomew Cubbins saw him trapped there, stuck to three stew pots, a tea cup, and a cat! (Yowls) The Royal Laundress rushed outside to  save her laundry. (wails of alarm) Bartholomew saw her, stuck tight to the clothesline between two woolen stockings and the king's best Sunday blouse! (more screaming) (TWANG!) He saw the Royal Fiddlers. They were stuck to their royal fiddles. Everywhere Bartholomew ran he saw someone stuck to something! (slurpping and plaintiff wails of alarm) They were stuck up by the dozens every last friend he had in the world was flopping and floundering all hopelessly caught in the goo! Then suddenly midst the hubub, Bartholomew gasped. "The King!"  Where was the King? He'd forgotten all about him. It was in the throne room that Bartholomew found  him. There he sat... old King Derwin, proud and mighty ruler of the Kingdom of Didd, trembling, shaking, helpless as a baby. His royal crown was stuck to his royal head. The seat of his royal pants were stuck to his royal throne. Oobleck was dripping from his royal eyebrows. It was oozing into his royal ears. "Fetch my magicians, Bartholomew!" he commanded. "Make them say some magic words! Make them stop the oobleck falling!" Bartholomew shrugged his shoulders. I can't fetch them your majesty. Their cave on Mount Neeka-tave is buried deep in oobleck." "Then I must think of some magic words!" groaned the King. "Oh, what are those things those magic words those magicians say...? Shuffle... duffel...  muzzle... muff.... That's all I can remember and they don't do any good! The oobleck keeps falling harder!" Bartholomew Cubbins could hold his tongue no longer. "And it's going to keep on falling," he shouted, "until your whole great marble palace tumbles down! So don't waste your time saying foolish magic words. YOU ought to be saying some plain simple words!" "Simple words...?" What do you mean, boy?" "I mean," said  Bartholomew, "this is all YOUR fault! Now the least you can do is say the simple words, 'I'm sorry'." No one had ever talked to the king like this before. "What!" he bellowed. "Me... ME say I'm sorry! Kings never say 'I'm sorry!' And I'm the mightiest king in all  the world!" Bartholomew looked the King square  in the eye. "You may be a mighty king," he said, "But you're sitting in oobleck up to your chin. And so  is everyone else in your land. And if you won't even say you're sorry, you're no sort of king at  all! Bartholomew Cubbins turned his back. He started for the throne room door. But then Bartholomew  heard a great deep sob. The old King was crying! (sobbing) "Come back Bartholomew Cubbins!" You're right! It's all my fault! And I am sorry! Oh, Bartholomew, I'm awfully, awfully sorry!" And the moment the king spoke those words, something happened... Maybe there WAS something magic  in those simple words, "I'm sorry." Maybe there WAS something magic in those simple words, "it's all my fault." Maybe there was, and maybe there wasn't. But they say that as soon as the old King spoke them, the sun began to shine and fight its way through the storm. They say that the falling oobleck drops  grew smaller and smaller and smaller... and smaller. They say that all the oobleck that was stuck on  all the people, and all the animals of the Kingdom   of Didd just simply, quietly melted away. And, they  say, Bartholomew took the old King by the sleeve ... ...and led him up the steps of the high bell tower. He  put the bell rope into His Majesty's royal hands,  and the King himself rang the holiday bell. Then the King proclaimed a brand-new national holiday... in honor of the four perfect things that came down from the sky. The King now knew that these four old-fashioned  things ...the rain, the sunshine, the fog and the snow... were good enough for any king in all the world, especially for him, old King Derwin of Didd. That's the story of the terrible green oobleck, that fell out of the sky on everybody's head, and everybody's cows, and everybody's houses. And it was a giant terrible mess that they thought would take weeks to clean up. And all it took was for King Derwin to apologize. title: Jurassic Park For Kids - Story Time
fulltitle: Jurassic Park For Kids - Story Time
description:
This adventurous science fiction story from a movie is told for children so that young kids can enjoy the mystery and entertainment of an epic storytelling. Perfect for air travel or long roadtrips, Jurassic Park will ignite children's imaginations with a love of dinosaurs. 

I love going to the zoo... And I love dinosaurs. But you can't see Dinosaurs at the zoo... 

What if someone made a special zoo where all the animals were dinosaurs?
This is the story of Jurassic Park told for younger audiences to enjoy. People do get eaten, but with the same tone as the wolf eating Little Red Riding Hood's grandmother. Children will find references to various species of dinosaurs including Brontosaurus, Hadrosaurus, Triceratops, Dilophosaurus, Velociraptor, and Tyrannosaurus Rex.  Kids will also be exposed to concepts like Paleontology and its basic history, DNA and its role in helping bodies grow, how zoos work behind the scenes, and many references to herd animals like Cows, Zebras, Wildebeest, Elephants, and big cats like lions, tigers, leopards, and cheetahs. There's heavy encouragement to interest young kids in reading nonfiction science books about animals and especially dinosaurs which can get a lot of boys who think they don't like reading to enjoy it. This story is full of adventure and will help young children develop a longer attention span as they learn to listen to a longer story than many picture books. 
I hope you enjoy this telling!

In this captivating read aloud, we follow the imaginative adventures of Clarinda, a young girl with a passion for butterflies. Through the power of her imagination, Clarinda discovers the courage to spread her wings and embark on a magical journey of self-discovery.

With vivid illustrations and heartfelt storytelling, "Clarinda Takes Flight" celebrates the importance of embracing our dreams, overcoming fears, and finding our unique voice. This educational travel story for children is about two farm animals who travel to visit the Queen of England in their DIY hot air balloon. This is a wonderful adventure story about scientific exploration and invention for young girls and boys and will open the world to their young minds. CLARINDA TAKES FLIGHT – By Robert Kinerk illustrated by Steven Kellog
Smash that like button if this stands out to you and please share it if it's really worthwhile! 

In this wonderful story, three friends explore the wonders of flight to try and access the skies by airplane, rocket, helicopter, and finally by hot air balloon. They end up drifting off over the Atlantic ocean to the United Kingdom where they get to meet the Queen of England herself and be knighted. They borrow some tea to take home to their friend and launch themselves back across the ocean to their humble beginnings where they enjoy a happy reunion. 


Once again I'd like to say that reading and vocabulary are essential tools to your child's future. Written and spoken words are tools by which we perceive, think, ponder, share, and communicate. Reading to your kids exposes them to words our everyday conversation eliminates. The richness of our speech is on a constant decline as we value simplicity and brevity over the richness available in the English language. Reading stories broadens your child's exposure to the world. It builds an understanding of who they are and who they can someday become as they're given examples of different character traits and choose which ones they admire and which they do not. It builds the richness of your child's imagination. It gives them settings and situations to use in their play. Reading to your children helps them grow up. Most importantly it teaches your children how much you love them by the time you spend with them sharing these experiences. Opening the world of a single story to your child is one of the greatest gifts you can give. I know many families don't have a tradition of reading bedtime stories or reading in the car on road trips. I feel fortunate that I was raised by a Mom and a Dad who had favorite stories and would spend time with us reading. I think I was 6 years old when Dad began reading the Lion, The Witch, and the Wardrobe to us. Once we finished that, he moved on to Prince Caspian and then the next and the next until we finished all seven books from The Chronicles of Narnia by C.S, Lewis. These were special memories he built with us. My Mom would read to us great stories like Farm Boy, and The Sign of the Beaver. These books broadened our imaginations as small boys. We admired the characters from the stories as well as the rich historical context they brought into our everyday playing.

Read aloud bedtime story for children who might struggle with feeling grumpy. Let this picture book help add some humor to your perspective. 
😡 Get ready to meet the crankiest character in town in our read aloud of "Crankenstein"! 📖🌪️

In this uproariously funny story, we follow the adventures of Crankenstein—a creature who wakes up on the wrong side of the bed every single day. From gloomy Mondays to tangled shoelaces, Crankenstein's grumpiness knows no bounds. But will something unexpected bring a smile to Crankenstein's face?

Join us as we bring "Crankenstein" to life through animated storytelling and vibrant illustrations. This laugh-out-loud read aloud will have kids of all ages giggling and relating to those moments when everything seems to go wrong. Through Crankenstein's journey, we learn that even the grumpiest of days can turn around.

Don't miss out on this hilarious adventure! Subscribe and hit that notification bell to join us for more entertaining read aloud sessions, engaging stories, and moments of laughter and joy. Let's dive into the pages of "Crankenstein" and discover the power of finding happiness even in the crankiest of moments! 🎉😄📚

Crankenstein is about when your attitude makes every bad thing in your day worse and you simply become a monster all day long. Hopefully, this story will make you laugh and help you choose to be happy even when the day is hard because you're special and you can make your family and friends have a better day if you try. 
Crankenstein - By Samantha Berger and Dan Santat - Read Aloud - Bedtime Story for kids

The day starts out bad when Mom comes in to wake him up and the sunlight pouring through the windows is just too much. It burns his eyes! 
He gets up and goes into the kitchen for breakfast only to find someone has eaten all the maple syrup. So he has to put up with eating his pancakes dry. Terrible. Then it's time for school. The bus pulls up and he almost can't get up and go get on it. Then it starts raining. Nothing is worse than recess in the rain. He's not happy at all. It reminds him of the other times he's turned into Crankenstein. There was that Halloween when it was so cold outside he had to wear a scarf over the front of his robot costume. There was the time during that summer heat wave that he couldn't even finish a popsicle before the burning sun would melt it all over his hand leaving a horrible sticky mess! There was the time he went to the fair with his parents and wanted to go ride the big roller coaster because he was finally tall enough as the sign said. Still, instead of flapping his arms while flying up and down in the air, he got to stand in a long long line for hours and hours of a hot afternoon listening to people in line brag about how dumb they were. He remembered getting sick last year and having to take that disgusting Dr. Giggles Cough Syrup for kids. It tasted like batteries and old lady deodorant. Terrible. And then there's every night when he finally finishes his homework and gets to settle down and watch a few episodes of his favorite TV show that Mom or Dad will end it early and tell him to go to bed. It's too much for a kid to take! So this particular day at school, when his Optimus Prime action figure suddenly becomes headless, Crankenstein must come forth once more! The boy screams in agony as the rage takes over! Nothing is fair! Nothing is right in the world! How can everything conspire against him so completely!? Well, at that same moment a little girl in his class undergoes the same transformation because her pet unicorn has the same neck attachment issue and everything in her life is even worse than in his because her Mom forgot to buy milk and so she had dry shredded wheat for breakfast! Nothing in the world is worse than dry shredded wheat! Cows can't even enjoy it!
Well, the glimpse of each other's faded countenances, their sobbing eyes, and running noses strikes each kid as equally hilarious and they both burst out laughing uncontrollably. And just like that, they're off again to play and swing and skip and howl, because even though kids have a terrible monster inside there's also a pretty fantastic little person growing up too.'

Kermit the Hermit has a huge collection of things. Will he ever give up his treasure to help anyone else? 
#readaloudbooksforkids #kidlit #bedtimestories #kids #kidsvideo #learntoread #childrensbooks #kidslearningvideos #kidsstories #readalong #TGABS #cartoonanimals #booktuber 
This is a wonderful story that takes children on a  wild adventure from the mayhem of seagulls on the bay to the struggles of crabs in the tide pools, the massive collection Kermit hides in his castle in the rocks, to fishing and beach combing across the sand dunes, as well as discovering shipwrecks and treasure in the deep ocean where the sharks are, all the way up to flying high through the air above the whole expanse. It's a beautifully illustrated story well told, that I hope you and your children will enjoy over and over again. 
This is a Bill Peet storybook for children about sea creatures at the beach in Monterey Bay. Perhaps you've visited the waterfront or an aquarium and seen some of the animals in this picture book. It's a tale about a terribly selfish crab who learns to be generous and friendly after a harrowing experience. He fights with seagulls for his food and collection items, but finally tangles with a dog and after pinching his nose, the dog decides to bury him in the sand for good. But a boy comes along and rescues him. This makes Kermit want to pay the boy back somehow but he doesn't think any of the objects in his collection would be suitable for a boy. He tries to help the boy catch big fish, but the halibut he finds is so huge, the line snaps, and Kermit is hauled out to the deep ocean where he sinks down to a shipwreck of an old treasure fleet. He's attacked by a blue shark and hides inside a chest filled with gold coins. After the shark gets tired of bruising his nose and leaves, Kermit decides to smuggle the treasure back to his castle in the rocks two gold coins at a time, one in each claw. He makes the trip over and over again till he stashes all of it in his cave. Then with the help of a pelican, he flies the gold to the boy's house and drops it down the stove pipe one coin at a time. The family never discovers their benefactor, but are very grateful. They use the money from the treasure to buy a TV set and dolls for the girl and bikes for the boys, then they wisely save the rest of the money.

In this episode, get ready for a sizzling and hilarious adventure as we read aloud "Dragons Love Tacos 2" by Adam Rubin.

Join us as we embark on a journey with our fiery friends, the dragons, who have an insatiable appetite for tacos. In this much-anticipated sequel, we reunite with our dragon pals as they face a taco tragedy of epic proportions. With engaging storytelling and vibrant illustrations, "Dragons Love Tacos 2" takes us on a taco-filled quest that's sure to keep kids of all ages captivated.

As we read aloud, you'll experience the joy of sharing this imaginative tale about friendship, courage, and, of course, tacos. Laugh along with the witty dialogue and hilarious mishaps that unfold, as our dragon heroes navigate through time to save the taco party. Will they triumph and restore taco goodness to the world?

Gather the little ones, find a comfy spot, and get ready for a fun-filled reading adventure. We'll bring the story to life, infusing it with animated voices, expressive storytelling, and interactive moments. Kids will have a chance to engage with the story, answer questions, and immerse themselves in the taco-filled universe created by Adam Rubin.

Whether you're a long-time fan of "Dragons Love Tacos" or discovering the series for the first time, this read aloud is a delightful experience for the whole family. It's perfect for bedtime stories, family storytime, or simply enjoying quality time together with a touch of taco-themed magic.

Join us as we read aloud "Dragons Love Tacos 2" by Adam Rubin, and let the adventure begin! 3 Points to help build interest in reading:
Choice and Access: Offer children a wide variety of books and reading materials to choose from, catering to their interests and reading levels. Create a well-stocked bookshelf or visit the library together to allow them to explore different genres, authors, and subjects. Giving children the autonomy to select their own books fosters a sense of ownership and excitement about reading.

Read Aloud and Share: Engage in regular read-aloud sessions where you read to your child or take turns reading together. Choose captivating books with interesting characters and plots to capture their attention. Make it an interactive experience by discussing the story, asking open-ended questions, and encouraging them to share their thoughts and predictions. By making reading a shared experience, you foster a love for storytelling and create memorable moments together.

Create a Reading Routine: Establishing a consistent reading routine can help children develop a habit of reading. Set aside dedicated time each day for reading, whether it's in the morning, before bed, or during a quiet afternoon. Make it a part of their daily routine, just like brushing their teeth or having meals. Consistency and predictability in reading habits can instill a sense of discipline and reinforce the importance of reading in their lives.

By implementing these strategies, you can help children build a genuine interest in reading, expanding their imagination, language skills, and knowledge. Remember, cultivating a love for reading is a gradual process, so be patient, and encouraging, and celebrate their reading milestones along the way.
